# City symphony — Style Prompt

> A place cut like a piece of minimalist music. Time-lapse turns traffic into rivers of light, people into ghosts and then into tracks of sodium light, clouds into water; every cut lands on the beat grid and the cuts get denser as the piece builds. One shot is held a whole bar (the brake) while the day ring in the corner freezes, the last bar runs the day backwards in 4-frame cuts, and the film stops on a hard cut to black on the bar line. It ends where it began, on the same camera at the next dawn, darkened, with the closing words. No narrator, few words, all set left-aligned on a soft darkening, never on a box, under a 35 mm release-print grade.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **An edit style.** The picture is the place itself: one high camera over the city, a plaza from above, a station clock, a corridor, a street from straight above, a hall full of people, street canyons. The look lives in *how time is bent* and *where the cuts fall*, not in a drawn style. In Mosio every shot is painted once (seeded canvas, then an image) and only moved, so it reads as footage: depth from perspective, light from gradients, texture from grain.
- **The beat grid is the script.** Every time comes from one function, `B(bar, beat)`. The example runs at 96 BPM (the source's 120 BPM slowed 1.25× to fit 15 s): beat 0.625 s, bar 2.5 s. Arc: one bar on the opening camera, then two beats per place, the clock punched in on its last beat, the brake (one bar), one street per beat with punch-ins on half beats, the flashback, a hard stop on the bar line, the coda.
- **Machines fast, people slow.** Vehicles, clouds and light are sped up until they become lines and drifts; people appear as crowds, as ghosts (a corridor ramps from 1× to 6× and the walkers smear into faded copies), or as tracks of light. Slow a thing, never a face.
- **One camera is the clock.** The same high camera opens (night turning into dawn in a third of a second, a 40× time-lapse), ends the flashback (night and dawn flickering every 2 frames) and carries the coda (the next dawn). A thin 24-hour day ring in the corner runs with the film's day.
- **It is not** a travel reel on a pop track, a vlog, a news package, a narrated explainer, a slideshow of postcards. No lower thirds with people's names, no centred title cards, no page-turn or zoom transitions, no logo sting, no dissolves between shots.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Footage, painted.** Each shot is one full-frame plate drawn once from a seeded PRNG at 0.75 scale (footage is soft; fewer pixels to paint) and shown as an image: perspective boxes with window grids for buildings, a herringbone brick plaza laid in affine strips through a wide-lens projection, a one-point-perspective corridor, a top-down street with a 9,000-dot crowd strip, a station clock in SVG. What moves sits on its own layer: the light streaks, the crowd strip, the track layers, the cloud sheet, the ghost version of the corridor.
- **35 mm release print** over everything: a 1.85:1 matte (21 px bars on 1920×1080); lifted blacks (screen 2%), warm highlights (soft-light of `--utama` at 13%) and saturation 0.86 baked into each plate; a vignette of 16% at the edge midpoints and 39% in the corners; clumped grain (a 640×360 noise image at 3.3×, opacity 0.4, re-placed every frame); gate weave ±0.5 px.
- **Light river**: a static bloom along the avenue (strokes of 34/15/6/2 px) plus two dashed strokes running in opposite directions, about 700 px a second.
- **Ghosts**: a walker painted as 4 copies of one silhouette, 9 px apart (scaled with depth), at opacity 0.6 → 0.2, the frame blending of a 360° shutter; sharp walkers are one copy.
- **Tracks** (people as data): chains of 8-20 positions, a dot of radius 3 at each and a 2 px line between them, in sodium lifted 25% toward white, with no depth scaling, drawn on two layers; the plate under them turns grey and dark (to 38%).
- **Shade, not boxes**: legibility comes from a soft Gaussian darkening of `--latar` behind the text block (centre 560, 830; radii 780 × 270; 62% at the centre), and from putting text over the darker part of the frame.
- Never generated images or photographs of real places; no live 3D. No outlines, no flat cartoon fills: plates stay soft and believable.

## 3. Colour logic

| Role | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sodium light: light rivers, crowd tracks, the rule under every number, the day ring's dot and arc, the source line of the quote | `--utama` (`--natrium` = 85% `--utama` + print white, for light) | the only accent of the film; the brand's main colour takes it. Script lifts it toward white when the brand's main colour is too dark to glow |
| Type | `--teks` | warm white (#EDE8DF) in the film's own colours |
| Secondary lines (labels, sources, years), the day ring | `--teks-redup` | #B0AAA0 |
| The darkening behind text, the end darkening (to 22%) | `--latar` (`--kabut` = alpha 0.62 on a dark brand, up to 0.94 on a white one) | a pale brand gets a soft white haze and dark text |
| Rules, the ring's dot and arc, the quote's source line | `--utama-di-latar` | they sit on the shade |
| Matte bars and the cut to black | `--matte` = film black mixed 10% toward `--latar` | stays dark under every brand |
| Footage colours | fixed look tokens: night sky, dawn, concrete, brick, stone, foliage, steel, window light, day sky, morning gold, print white and black | they are the city; only the warm grade follows the brand |

`--aksen` appears only as one colour among the corridor's ad panels. The brand never appears as a box.

## 4. Type

- **Left-aligned, never centred, never on a box**, one line per item, never wrapped.
- **Number card** (lower left): the number in `--font-judul` 84 px, tracking 0.06 em, top at y 690, x 168 (a unit in 44 px capitals beside it); a 2 px rule in `--utama-di-latar` at y 806 that grows from x 172 to 560 px wide over 0.9 s, starting 0.2 s after the card; the line saying what it counts in `--font-isi` 28 px at y 826; a capitals line in `--font-judul` 16 px, tracking 0.25 em, `--teks-redup`, at y 874 (source or year). "About" numbers carry `≈`.
- **Title** (lower left): `--font-isi` 66 px at y 752, x 168, then a capitals line in `--font-judul` 20 px, tracking 0.32 em, at y 862.
- **Place or year label**: `--font-judul` 22 px capitals, tracking 0.3 em, bottom left at x 64, y 968.
- **Quote** (lower left): `--font-isi` 60 px at y 716, x 196; a 20 px capitals line at +112; a 14 px capitals source line in `--utama-di-latar` at +160.
- **End slate** (top left, x 196): `--font-isi` 54 px at y 244 with a 20 px capitals line beside it; a 640 px rule at y 350; `--font-isi` 26 px at y 376 with a 15 px capitals line beside it; 24 px at y 430.
- Families: a wide technical grotesque for the capitals and numbers (Space Grotesk 500 here; Inter 600 in capitals also works), a light neutral sans for the lines (Inter 400). The clock numerals belong to the picture (Libre Baskerville), not to the brand.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Cuts**: hard cuts only, all from `B()`. Opening camera 1 bar; plaza 2 beats; clock 1 beat, then the punch-in 1 beat; corridor 2 beats; street from above 2 beats; the brake 1 bar; streets 1 beat each with a ×1.16 punch-in on the half beat; flashback 8 shots × 4 frames, then night/dawn every 2 frames; hard stop on the bar line (12.5 s); 0.1 s of black; coda 2.4 s.
- **Camera per shot** (linear over the shot): opening 1.00 → 1.06 and up 8 px; plaza a pull-back 1.04 → 1.00; clock 1.00 → 1.04, punch-in 1.00 → 1.05; corridor 1.00 → 1.06; street from above and the hall static; coda 1.00 → 1.06 and up 6 px. Punch-ins are cuts to a tighter framing of the same shape, never zooms.
- **Night to dawn**: the night plate fades out over 0.35 s (`sine.inOut`) at 1.45 s, the light river keeps running.
- **Speed ramp**: the corridor's ghost version fades in from 0.15 s over 0.6 s (`power2.in`): sharp walkers smear into ghosts as the speed climbs from 1× to 6×.
- **Text**: cards appear in 0.12 s (the title in 0.3 s, its capitals line 0.25 s later) and leave on the cut with their shot; they may stay across cuts only while the shots under them are what they count. **Number lock** (counts, times): one digit locks every quarter beat while the others roll. **Count-up** (flows, crowds): 0 → n in 0.65 s, cubic ease-out.
- **The brake**: 0.15 s after the cut the plate turns grey over 0.4 s while the tracks appear (two layers 0.3 s apart, inside a circle opening from the floor's centre over 1 s); the day ring freezes and dims to 45%.
- **Day ring** at (1726, 948), radius 40: 24 ticks (6 px at 00/06/12/18, 3 px otherwise), labels 00 06 12 18 in 11 px, a sodium dot on the rim with the last three hours as a 3 px arc behind it. It fades in over 0.3 s, turns 60° → 150° by the brake, freezes, turns on to 195°, and in the flashback spins back to 60° (`power1.out`).
- **Ending**: from black, the coda fades up in 0.15 s; the shot is darkened to 22% and keeps moving; the quote and the slate fade in within 0.15 s each (0.05-0.1 s apart) and the slate's rule grows in 0.25 s; everything is still from 12.95 s to the end.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| The high camera, slow push 1.00 → 1.06 | the whole place before anything happens | the hook, a title, a date |
| Same camera, night fading into dawn in 0.35 s (40× time-lapse) | time passing without a caption | "before the city wakes", opening hours, a season |
| Cut on the beat to a new place, slow push or pull-back of 4-6% | the place in parts, the rhythm of a day | facts, steps, stations of a route |
| Punch-in cut to a tighter framing of the same shape | insistence, the beat getting denser | the time that matters, a sign, a product detail |
| Speed ramp 1× → 6× on a crowd: sharp people smear into ghosts | the day speeding up | a rush hour, a launch, a busy season |
| Top-down, a strip flowing through a static frame | volume, many people or things | crowds, orders, members, traffic |
| The brake: one static shot for a bar, people turning into tracks of light | stop and look at what all the movement adds up to | the key number, the proof, the route |
| Reverse flashback, 4-frame cuts, ending on a 2-frame night/dawn flicker | the whole day rewinding | the recap before the call to action |
| Hard cut to black on a bar line | the full stop | the end of the story before the offer |
| Back to the opening camera, darkened to 22%, text held still | the circle closing | the call to action, the closing quote |

## 7. Native moves

- **Light river.** An avenue seen from high above at night, a static bloom plus dashed streaks running both ways. *Fits content like:* a night market opening at dusk; a courier service that runs till midnight; a creator's channel about night walks; the opening of a story in a city that never sleeps.
- **Night into dawn on one camera.** The same position, the night plate fading out in a third of a second; later the flashback ends on night and dawn flickering every 2 frames. *Fits content like:* a bakery's 4 a.m. start; a gym open 24 hours; a photography class on golden hour; a short story that begins before sunrise.
- **Punch-in with a locking number.** A shape (a clock, a sign, a product) cut tighter on the beat while a time or count locks digit by digit in the lower left. *Fits content like:* "05.00" for a running club; a shop's opening time; the date of a workshop; the minute a story turns.
- **Ramp to ghosts.** A crowd shot speeds from 1× to 6× and its people smear into faded copies. *Fits content like:* a market's morning rush; visitors on an open day; a creator's studio over a day; a school corridor between classes.
- **Crowd to count.** A static top-down street with a flowing crowd strip while a count-up states how many. *Fits content like:* 312 runners every Sunday; members of a community; orders on launch day; students who finished a course.
- **Crowd to tracks (the brake).** One static bar: the plate turns grey and where people walk lights up in sodium dot chains; the day ring freezes. *Fits content like:* the 42 km of a club's routes; a delivery area mapped by its trips; a teacher's year as paths; the routes of a story's characters crossing.
- **Reverse flashback and hard stop.** Earlier shots return backwards, 4 frames each, then the film cuts to black on the bar. *Fits content like:* the recap before a sign-up; a week of a shop in one second; a vlog's highlights; the last beat of a story.
- **The bookend.** The opening camera at the next dawn, darkened to 22%: a quote lower left, the slate top left. *Fits content like:* a club's meeting point and chat; a shop's address; a class's sign-up line; the closing line of a story.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Never a box behind text.** Use the Gaussian shade and place cards over the darker part of the shot; move a card to a darker shot rather than set it on a white floor or sky.
- **Cuts off the grid** feel like a slideshow. Derive every time from `B()`; never type an arbitrary length. The slowest shot sits at the brake.
- **Too much light.** A night city with every window lit turns into a grey field: keep about 4% of windows lit and let a few blocks and the avenue carry the light; walls stay near black.
- **Tracks as a web.** Long continuous lines read as a map, not as people: keep chains short, with a dot at every position.
- **Illustration creep.** Outlines, flat cartoon fills, bouncing eases or characters break the footage illusion. Keep gradients, perspective, grain and linear camera moves.
- **Faces as heroes.** Do not make an identifiable person the slowed or close-up subject: people are crowds, ghosts or tracks.
- **Performance and load.** Paint plates once at reduced scale and turn them into images; keep animated layers (light river, tracks, darkening) on their own compositor layers; hide shots that are off screen (`autoAlpha: 0`); change the clock's framing through its `viewBox`.
- **Initial states.** A layer that fades in later (the ghost corridor, the tracks) must start hidden in CSS: a `fromTo` that does not render immediately leaves it visible until it starts.
- **Numbers.** Two to four number cards at most; give a source or year for each, and only real figures the user provides.
- **Dead endings.** Never end on black: the coda shot keeps moving under the closing text, which holds at least 2 s.

# City symphony: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 0.625, medium 1.25, long 2.5.

## hook

- en: one high camera over the place, the avenue a river of light; night fades into dawn in 0.35 s; title set lower left on a soft shade
- id: satu kamera tinggi di atas kota, jalan jadi sungai cahaya; malam jadi fajar dalam sekejap; judul rata kiri bawah di atas bayang lembut

## problem

- en: one shot held a whole bar, the day ring freezes and dims; a short line lower left names what is missing
- id: satu shot ditahan satu birama, cincin hari membeku dan redup; satu baris di kiri bawah menyebut apa yang kurang

## fact

- en: a cut on the beat to the place, then a punch-in on the same shape; a time or date locks digit by digit lower left
- id: potong di ketukan ke tempatnya, lalu pukul-masuk ke bentuk yang sama; jam atau tanggal terkunci per digit di kiri bawah

## step

- en: one shot per beat with a punch-in on the half beat; the stage name and distance in small spaced capitals bottom left
- id: satu shot tiap ketukan, pukul-masuk di setengah ketukan; nama tahap dan jaraknya kecil berjarak di kiri bawah

## compare

- en: counterpoint split: two halves of the same kind of place (then and now, night and day), the gutter grows from the centre
- id: layar terbelah: dua tempat sejenis (dulu dan kini, malam dan siang), celah tumbuh dari tengah

## number

- en: the brake: one static bar, the shot turns grey and people become sodium dot chains; the number locks with a growing rule
- id: rem: satu birama diam, gambar memudar abu-abu, orang jadi rantai titik cahaya; angka terkunci, garis tumbuh

## proof

- en: a crowd speeds from 1× to 6× until people smear into ghosts, or flows top-down; a count-up states how many
- id: kerumunan dipercepat 1× sampai 6× hingga orang jadi bayang, atau mengalir dari atas; jumlahnya dihitung naik

## offer

- en: a grid of shots on the beat, 1×2 then 2×2 then 3×3; the offer set left in wide capitals over the darkest cell
- id: kisi shot di ketukan, 1×2 lalu 2×2 lalu 3×3; penawaran kapital lebar rata kiri di sel paling gelap

## cta

- en: the day runs backwards in 4-frame cuts, hard cut to black, then the opening camera darkened: name and contact top left, held 2 s
- id: hari diputar mundur cepat, potong keras ke hitam, lalu kamera pembuka digelapkan: nama dan kontak kiri atas, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: hard cut to black on the bar, then the opening camera at the next dawn, darkened, under one closing line, held 2 s
- id: potong keras ke hitam di birama, lalu kamera pembuka di fajar berikutnya, digelapkan, satu kalimat penutup, diam 2 detik
